name: What should I do if my bathroom remodel is taking much longer than promised?

mainEntity.name: What should I do if my bathroom remodel is taking much longer than promised?

acceptedAnswer.text: If the project falls behind, first identify whether the cause is design changes, inspections, material delays, concealed repairs, labor availability, or incomplete work. Then ask for a revised sequence with specific decisions and dates rather than accepting a vague promise to finish soon. Elite Remodeling & Design’s process can involve several connected stages, so delays in selections, permits, or inspections may affect construction. Key factors include: - Long-lead fixtures and tile - Unresolved change orders - Failed or pending inspections - Work that cannot proceed until another trade finishes. Keep a written decision log and respond promptly to requests for approvals. Ask which tasks can continue safely while the delayed item is resolved and how the revised completion date is calculated.
acceptedAnswer.description: Ask for the specific cause, unfinished scope, pending decisions, inspection status, material updates, and a revised written schedule. Separate owner changes from contractor delays, document communications, and confirm which tasks can proceed while the blocked item is resolved.
